title: Kinds of jurisdiction of a civil court

cards.title: Subject-matter (inherent)
cards.text: The kind of dispute: suits of a civil nature (s. 9). Lack of it makes a decree a nullity; consent cannot cure it.

cards.title: Pecuniary
cards.text: Money value: s. 6 CPC; DJ unlimited (s. 7 Ordinance); Civil Judges as fixed by IHC (s. 9).

cards.title: Territorial
cards.text: Geographical area: ss. 16–20 CPC; local limits fixed by IHC (s. 10 Ordinance). Objection waivable (s. 21).

cards.title: Original
cards.text: Trying a case at first instance: suits and original petitions.

cards.title: Appellate
cards.text: Hearing appeals: ss. 96–108 CPC; ss. 17–18 Ordinance.

cards.title: Revisional
cards.text: Correcting jurisdictional errors where no appeal lies: s. 115 CPC (High Court and District Court).

cards.title: Exclusive
cards.text: Only one forum can try: e.g. Family Court, Rent Controller — civil court barred.

cards.title: Concurrent
cards.text: Several courts can try: plaintiff chooses; s. 15 lowest grade; s. 22 transfer.

cards.title: Inherent powers
cards.text: s. 151: orders for ends of justice / to prevent abuse — with reasons (Islamabad 2020). Supplements, never creates, jurisdiction.

title: Is the civil court's jurisdiction barred? (s. 9 CPC)

q.ask: Is the suit of a civil nature — does it involve a civil right (property, office, status, contract, tort)?
q.yes: Go to question 2. Religious questions do not matter if property or office is in issue (Explanation).
q.no: Not maintainable under s. 9 (purely religious, social or political question).

q.ask: Does a statute EXPRESSLY bar civil courts ("no civil court shall entertain …")?
q.yes: Barred — unless the act complained of falls in question 4.

q.ask: Is there an IMPLIED bar — a statute creating a new right with its own complete remedy, or public policy?
q.yes: Barred — unless the act complained of falls in question 4.
q.no: Civil court HAS jurisdiction (presumption under s. 9).

q.ask: Was the special forum's act without jurisdiction, mala fide, coram non judice, or against natural justice / not under the Act at all?
q.yes: Civil court CAN examine it despite the ouster clause (Mask & Co.; Abbasia Cooperative Bank PLD 1997 SC 3).
q.no: Civil court cannot interfere; use the remedies in the special statute.

q.ask: Is the suit about immovable property (recovery, partition, mortgage, other right, wrong to it)?
q.yes: Sue where the property is (s. 16); mortgage suits also where cause of action arose; personal-obedience relief also where defendant resides (proviso); several districts — any (s. 17).

q.ask: Is it for compensation for a wrong to the person or to movable property?
q.yes: Plaintiff may sue where the wrong was done OR where the defendant resides / works (s. 19).

q.ask: Any other suit (contract, money, declaration, etc.)
q.yes: Where the defendant (each, or any with leave / acquiescence) resides, carries on business or works for gain, OR where the cause of action wholly or partly arose (s. 20). Corporation: principal or subordinate office (Expl. II).
q.no: Check any special law (Family Courts Act, rent laws) for its own territorial rule.

q.yes: The lowest grade competent to try it (s. 15), within its pecuniary limits (s. 6).
q.no: Objection to place of suing: take it in the trial court before issues (s. 21).

children.title: 1. Same matter
children.text: Directly and substantially in issue in both suits — actually or constructively (Expl. III, IV)

children.title: 2. Same parties
children.text: Or parties under whom they claim (privies); representative suits (Expl. VI)

children.title: 3. Same title
children.text: Litigating in the same capacity in both suits

children.title: 4. Competent court
children.text: Former court competent to try the later suit; appeal rights irrelevant (Expl. II)

children.title: 5. Heard and finally decided
children.text: Decided on merits and final; 'former' = decided first (Expl. I)

steps.title: Personal service
steps.text: On defendant, his authorised agent, business manager, or adult male family member residing with him

steps.title: Registered post A/D (simultaneous)
steps.text: Acknowledgment or postal refusal endorsement = prima facie proof

steps.title: Affixation
steps.text: Defendant refuses / not found after due diligence; identifiers named; officer examined

steps.title: Substituted service by court order
steps.text: Affixing at last residence, electronic means, courier, beat of drum, press, any mode — simultaneously

steps.title: Special cases
steps.text: Other district, prison, abroad, public officers, soldiers; letter instead of summons

title: Order IX — who is absent, what follows, what is the remedy

cards.title: Neither party appears (r. 3) / process fee unpaid (r. 2)
bullets: Remedy: fresh suit (limitation permitting) or restoration on sufficient cause (r. 4)

cards.title: Summons unserved, no step for 3 months (r. 5)
Plaintiff present, defendant absent (r. 6)
bullets: Served: ex parte; decree may be passed without evidence
Not served: fresh summons; served late: postpone
Before decree: join on good cause (r. 7)

cards.title: Defendant present, plaintiff absent (r. 8)
bullets: Suit dismissed (decree on any admitted part)
No fresh suit (r. 9); restore on sufficient cause — Art. 163, 30 days

cards.title: Ex parte decree (r. 13)
bullets: Set aside if summons not duly served OR sufficient cause
Not for mere irregularity if defendant knew the date
Art. 164: 30 days from decree / knowledge; s. 5 LA applies
